name: Scottsdale
question_title: Can you drive a golf cart in Scottsdale?
answer_short: Neighborhood electric vehicles yes, plain golf carts no. In Scottsdale, a registered neighborhood electric vehicle may use a road posted 35 mph or less and may cross a faster road. The city describes a golf cart as crossing a road for golf play, not as a street network.

golf_cart.roads: Not on public roads, except a crossing for golf play
golf_cart.notes: The city page does not open city streets to plain golf carts

lsv.notes: Registered and insured. Not on Loop 101.

rules.rule: A neighborhood electric vehicle shall not be driven on a highway posted over 35 mph, except to cross at an intersection.
On a golf course, no street registration is required. The city says a golf cart may cross the roadway for golf play.
rules.citation: City of Scottsdale alternative transportation page

faq.q: Where can I drive my LSV in Scottsdale?
faq.a: Roads posted 35 mph or less. Registered and insured. Not on Loop 101. A town or county can still ban LSVs from a specific road, and posted signs win.

faq.q: Can I drive a regular golf cart on city streets in Scottsdale?
faq.a: The city page does not allow that. It says a golf cart may cross a roadway for golf play.

faq.q: Can a neighborhood electric vehicle use Scottsdale Road?
faq.a: Only where it is posted 35 mph or less. Much of it is posted higher. Loop 101 is closed.
